newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-North in big iron ore expansion.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-North in big iron ore expansion.

text.p: Australian mining and forestry group North Ltd announced on Friday a major expansion of its iron ore operations, revealing it had bought control of Canada's biggest producer for US$230 million.
News of the group's 59.3 percent stake in the Iron Ore Co. of Canada (IOCC) came as North reported a 55 percent rise in half year net profit, ending a prolonged earnings slump.
North said the purchase, which will be funded from existing debt facilties, was a good fit, giving it access to a growing market that doesn't compete with its existing iron ore business.
"This purchase will complement our interest in Robe River and positions North as major player in the world's iron ore industry," North managing director Campbell Anderson told a news conference.

The acquisition would also provide North with an opportunity to capitalise on fast-growing electric arc furnace, or mini-mill, steel markets in the U.S. and Asia via reactivating an idle pellet plant at Sept-lles in Quebec province.
Iron ore pellets are used as supplementary feed for electric arc furnace steelmaking.
IOCC produces over 15 million tonnes a year of iron ore pellets and concentrates and employs over 2,400 people.
But North said it wants to continue to pare costs at the 40-year-old operation and would be reducing the current workforce and reducing cash costs of US$0.47 per iron tonne unit by US$0.10.

"There is considerable scope for workplace practice reform and productivity improvement. Profit improvement programmes are already being put in place. North will support this initiative and encourage capital investement," North executive director development Dick Knight said.
Knight added that it would take an investment of about US$77 million to achieve the cash cost target.
Analysts said news of the buy was not a great surprise as market rumours previously had abounded, but they were cautious about North's cost reduction ambitions.
"Clearly they have ideas on how to reduce costs but (they are) certainly not convincing. They may be able to, but it's early days," Bell Securities analyst Rob Craigie told Reuters.
IOCC's North America sales would continue to be made under long term contracts, primarily with Bethlehem Steel Co, National Steel Co and Dofasco Inc, North said.
North said its IOCC stake would be made up of Bethlehem Steel's 37.6 percent and National Steel's 21.7 percent holdings.
They will receive US$145 million and US$85 million respectively for their stakes.

Analysts were happy with North's A$50 million half year profit figure, but most said the focus was now on its 1997/98 prospects following the company's forecast that its full year results would be little changed from those of fiscal 1995/96.
"The half-year result was excellent," said Umit Safak, analyst at HSBC James Capel.
National Mutual Funds Managment analyst Bill Murray said: "The benefits are coming through in the next year. Next year is the more important one."
North said on Friday it was expecting a near-term upturn in iron ore, uranium, zinc and gold output and stronger sales of mining equipment spares.
-- Melbourne bureau 61-3 9286-1435
